newsitem.title: USA: Bottle deposit bill introduced in U.S. Senate.
newsitem.headline: Bottle deposit bill introduced in U.S. Senate.

text.p: A bill that would impose a nation-wide 10-cent deposit fee on beverage bottles and cans was introduced Tuesday by Sen. James Jeffords, who said it would reduce waste and encourage recycling.

"I firmly believe that deposit laws are a common sense, proven method to increase recycling, save energy, create jobs and decrease the generation of waste and proliferation of overflowing landfills," Jeffords, a Vermont Republican, said as he introduced the bill.
Jeffords said in Vermont, which has a bottle deposit law, the recycling rate was over 90 percent and was over 70 percent in nine other states with deposit fees.
"The concept of a national bottle bill is simple: to provide the consumer with an incentive to return the container for reuse or recycling," Jeffords said.

His bill would impose a 10-cent deposit on beer, soft-drink and water containers in states which have a beverage container recovery rate of less than 70 percent. Retailers would receive two cents per container for participating in the programme.
Similar container deposit bills have been introduced in previous sessions of Congress but have never passed because of opposition from the beverage industry.
